method.note: Live authorities remain canonical. This artifact is a compact research snapshot. US, Canada, Australia and ECB FX are required preflight inputs. NZ and Japan are not required_for_trader_preflight; a blocked RBNZ source or a Japan holiday-calendar print stays visible on that source and does not by itself mark the packet stale. NZ-dependent and JP-dependent expressions still fail closed. The official RBNZ B2 XLSX is tried first, including a browser-TLS retry, then the official RBNZ B2 HTML table. No vendor or media substitute is used. Japan JGB freshness uses the Tokyo business-day calendar and a one-session publication lag. Euro-area Bund (Germany) and Japan JGB cash curves remain six-economy rate legs. Cross-country spreads use exact common observation dates only. Policy-path context uses official overnight benchmarks plus public money-market data. The required tradable paper rates universe remains SOFR via CME SR3, CORRA via MX CRA, and AONIA via ASX IB. TONA is included when JPX OSE 3M settlements pass identity checks; FST3/€STR stays observe_only until a public settlement feed is reliable. Official government zero/forward curves are supplemental bond-curve inputs and are not required to manufacture a swap curve. Euro-area sovereign fragmentation (IT/FR/ES vs Bund) is market context, never an EA temperature input. Housing context is collected for the US, Canada and Australia from free maintained public sources: FHFA/Census/Fed/Freddie Mac via FRED for the US, Statistics Canada/CMHC/Bank of Canada for Canada, and ABS/RBA for Australia. EA/JP housing is omitted until an official/free source meets the contract. CFTC TFF supplies trader-class ownership/crowding context and can mark the packet stale. CME's public volume/open-interest service is a supplemental overlay and does not flip packet status. No historical warehouse is written to GitHub or Supabase.

items.headline: Trump tells UN he may 'annihilate' Iran or pursue a deal; Iran delegation walks out
items.summary: In his 22 Sep UNGA address, President Trump framed a binary choice between a rebuilding deal and rapid military annihilation of Iran, while tying the war to oil and politics; BBC/Reuters report much of the Iranian delegation left during the speech.

items.headline: US and Iran hold mediated UNGA talks on war end and Hormuz
items.summary: Al Jazeera reports hours of indirect US–Iran contact via mediators on 22 Sep; envoy Steve Witkoff said shuttling continued and Trump cited a lengthy, productive meeting involving Witkoff and Jared Kushner, though accounts differ on direct vs mediated contact.

items.headline: Senior Iranian official tells Reuters Hormuz could reopen in seven days if US eases blockade
items.summary: Reuters (Parisa Hafezi) on 22 Sep quoted a senior Iranian official saying the strait could reopen within seven days if Washington eases military pressure and lifts the port blockade, with Iran’s UN team described as fully empowered to revive diplomacy.

items.headline: Fars News disputes Reuters/Kyodo Hormuz reopening reports
items.summary: After the Reuters-sourced seven-day Hormuz story moved oil lower, Iran’s semi-official Fars cited sources calling those reports invalid/untrue; markets treated diplomacy hopes as tentative rather than confirmed policy.

items.headline: Saudi Arabia restarts East-West pipeline; Yanbu exports may resume
items.summary: Three industry sources told Reuters on 22 Sep that Saudi Arabia restarted the East-West pipeline at a low rate after the 11 Sep shutdown and could resume Red Sea loadings at Yanbu later Tuesday, with Aramco targeting higher flows over time.

items.headline: Oil holds near two-week lows as Gulf supply improves and Iran talks linger
items.summary: Reuters on 23 Sep reported Brent near ~$99.41/bbl in early London trade after Tuesday’s sub-$100 session, citing improving Gulf supply (Saudi pipeline, higher regional exports) alongside still-uncertain US–Iran diplomacy; prior-session Brent low cited near $97.36.

items.headline: Trump backs idea of US diesel export ban; Bessent says feasibility under review
items.summary: At UN meetings on 22 Sep, Trump said he supports halting diesel exports to ease record US pump prices; Treasury Secretary Bessent said officials are studying full vs partial restrictions, while Reuters analysts warned global market disruption.

items.headline: Wall Street mixed: Nasdaq closes at record as oil eases; Dow falls
items.summary: AP/Newser recap of 22 Sep US close: S&P 500 essentially flat (~7,764.64), Nasdaq +0.5% to a record ~27,244.28, Dow −185 points; banks weighed after the prior week’s Fed hike while the 10-year yield edged down toward ~4.95%.
